item.title: Katy ISD sets new framework on artificial intelligence use in classrooms
item.description:
- [Artificial Intelligence](https://abc13.com/tag/artificial-intelligence/)
# Katy ISD sets new framework on artificial intelligence use in classrooms KATY, Texas (KTRK) -- Leaders at Katy Independent School District say they've [established a framework for the use of artificial intelligence in classrooms](https://www.katyisd.org/news-details/board/news-headlines-katy-independent-school-district-100/post/katy-isd-strikes-a-balance-with-technology-and-ai-in-the-classroom) for the upcoming school year.
"Students will learn how to use AI," Assistant Superintendent Dr.
Bell, who presented the framework in front of the school board last week, called artificial intelligence "the current emerging technology of our times."
"Using it is changing how people work."
Katy ISD said it will phase the use of AI into classrooms based on grade level and is not intended to replace teachers or staff.
Those students will also be unable to use generative AI such as Google Gemini, but the district says that doesn't mean the technology is outright banned in those classrooms.
The distinction is important because certain District-approved programs use artificial intelligence to support reading instruction and personalize learning while remaining under teacher supervision."
Katy ISD said they will not use any AI platform that hasn't been reviewed and isn't compliant with federal education laws for protecting information.

item.title: LPL shares spike after CEO finally unveils his firm's artificial intelligence play, Cyan, to counter Hazel, after months of stock-price depression. It worked.
item.description:
# LPL shares spike after CEO finally unveils his firm's artificial intelligence play, Cyan, to counter Hazel, after months of stock-price depression. It worked. - LPL Financial unveils $2 billion AI overhaul, Cyan, boosting stock price. - Cyan offers agentic tools for advisors, automating tasks and providing insights. - AI integration aims to enhance advisor efficiency and client experiences. - LPL's AI strategy focuses on supporting, not replacing, human advisors.
AI generated
[LPL Financial](https://riabiz.com/tags/lpl-financial/page/1) today promised it has its eyes on artificial intelligence as part of a billion overhaul of its technology – and shares responded by shooting up more than $10 and nearer to where they traded when the Feb. 10 news of Altruist.
The Fort Mill, S.C.-based giant announced a do-it-all bundle for all advisor channels with “agentic” tools and the promise of 35 major technology enhancements.
The share climb of $10 was a leap of 3.22% to $342.40 today.
Still LPL made clear that those agentic improvements, branded as Cyan, are not in fact, client-facing agents but will play a subservient role to the 32,000 financial advisors who use LPL for clearing custody or as their in-house W-2 stockbrokers.
Still, the use of AI will be extensive including: Conversational workflow support, agentic automation for account maintenance, recommendations for practice growth and AI-generated financial planning.
“By creating a unified foundation across our business, we are accelerating innovation, unlocking the power of AI and data, and delivering more seamless, intelligent experiences for advisors and their clients."
[![LPL finally stops (largely) Anthropic-fueled stock price skid by confirming 'something big' -- with Anthropic -- a new Morningstar report pounding the table to buy LPL shares didn't hurt](https://riabiz.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fucarecdn.com%2F338d06ac-4e00-429b-b3b3-da43aaf1ec11%2F-%2Fformat%2Fwebp%2F-%2Fresize%2F120x120%2F-%2Fquality%2Fsmart%2F&w=3840&q=75)\ \ Related\ \ LPL finally stops (largely) Anthropic-fueled stock price skid by confirming 'something big' -- with Anthropic -- a new Morningstar report pounding the table to buy LPL shares didn't hurt](https://riabiz.com/a/2026/2/25/lpl-finally-stops-largely-anthropic-fueled-stock-price-skid-by-confirming-something-big-with-anthropic-a-new-morningstar-report-pounding-the-table-to-buy-lpl-shares-didnt-hurt)
Those capabilities vary from the Hazel capabilities of [Altruist](https://riabiz.com/tags/altruist/page/1), which sent shares spiraling across Wall Street but hit Schwab and LPL among the hardest.
[Hazel](https://riabiz.com/tags/hazel/page/1)'s big feature was AI tax planning, which interprets complex tax forms (like Form 1040s), pay stubs, and account data to create personalized tax strategies and real-time interactive scenario modeling.
LPL describes its plan for AI to “work behind the scenes to surface insights, automate routine tasks and support informed decisions.”
LPL made a prior announcement to let Wall Street it is on its toes with regard to AI on Feb. 24, two weeks after the [Hazel](https://riabiz.com/tags/hazel/page/1) announcement. See: [LPL finally stops (largely) Anthropic-fueled stock price skid by confirming 'something big' -- with Anthropic -- a new Morningstar report pounding the table to buy LPL shares didn't hurt](https://riabiz.com/a/2026/2/25/lpl-finally-stops-largely-anthropic-fueled-stock-price-skid-by-confirming-something-big-with-anthropic-a-new-morningstar-report-pounding-the-table-to-buy-lpl-shares-didnt-hurt)

item.title: IRS Office of Professional Responsibility Issues Introductory Guidelines on Artificial Intelligence Use in Federal Tax Practice
item.description: # IRS Office of Professional Responsibility Issues Introductory Guidelines on Artificial Intelligence Use in Federal Tax Practice On June 24, 2026, the IRS Office of Professional Responsibility (OPR) released 2026-19 (the OPR Guidance); its first substantive guidance on generative artificial intelligence (AI) in tax practice. The OPR Guidance notes there is no single settled definition of AI given how fast the technology changes, but describes it broadly as machines mimicking human cognitive functions, including judgment and prioritization and observes that virtually every tax firm already uses some form of it — often through research platforms such as Bloomberg Tax.

item.title: Grand County establishes position on artificial intelligence use
item.description:
# County establishes position on artificial intelligence use ![](https://swiftmedia.s3.amazonaws.com/mountain.swiftcom.com/images/sites/9/2026/05/25095612/AIcountyimage-1024x683.png)**A stock thumbnail image for AI stories created by Chat GPT.**
Most recently, the Grand County Board of County Commissioners answered the question of how they plan to [integrate artificial intelligence](https://www.skyhinews.com/news/grand-county-drafts-strategic-vision-for-use-of-ai/) into Grand County government technology systems in their [strategic AI Vision](https://drive.google.com/file/d/141QwuyFpC3Se1YTLwjVVJgyiyEuaZ_7-/view?usp=sharing).
Artificial intelligence is being embraced for administrative tasks, assistance to citizens and visitors, and consolidation of data sets. The county has laid out a plan for how it aims to integrate this new technology into the workflows of various departments.
Citizens and visitors will be notified when using artificial intelligence tools and personal data is said to be protected by advanced cybersecurity.
Moving forward, the board will establish an “AI Innovation Working Group” composed of department staff, elected officials and information technology professionals that will “incorporate regular community consultation and feedback mechanisms to identify “low-risk, high-impact” pilot projects for the 2027 fiscal year,” according to the document.

item.title: Dakota Intelligence brings artificial intelligence solutions to businesses
item.description:
# Dakota Intelligence brings artificial intelligence solutions to businesses ## Mitchell entrepreneur Timm Johnson helps organizations understand, adopt and implement AI Johnson uses artificial intelligence tools to develop solutions for businesses through Dakota Intelligence.
MITCHELL — Timm Johnson wants to make artificial intelligence less intimidating for South Dakota businesses.
Through his Mitchell-based company, Dakota Intelligence, Johnson builds AI systems that answer phones, automate paperwork and organize records.
Johnson operates Dakota Intelligence, an artificial intelligence consulting company that helps businesses adopt AI tools.
Operating from Mitchell, Dakota Intelligence focuses on helping farmers, small businesses, local governments and professional offices understand where artificial intelligence can improve daily operations — and where it cannot.
Since then, he has earned multiple artificial intelligence certifications through Anthropic Academy while working at Dakota Counseling Institute as a behavioral tech intake specialist and electronic health records super user.
During nearly three months at home, he immersed himself in artificial intelligence, studying developments and how those tools could benefit rural businesses.
The company builds AI-powered phone receptionists, appointment booking systems, workflow automation and digital operations dashboards.
A Make grid displays an interactive map of Timm Johnson’s artificial intelligence and no-code automation ecosystem.
He also insists every system include what he calls a "human in the loop," meaning people still review important decisions or content generated by artificial intelligence.
